title: India Biennale 2026: Dates, Venues, and What to Expect
seoTitle: India Biennale 2026: Delhi Dates, Venues and Pass Prices
excerpt: The India Biennale 2026 runs 4 December 2026 to 21 March 2027 in Delhi. Get the venues, pass types, rupee prices and booking details.
content:
The India Biennale 2026 is the second edition of India's large-scale contemporary art exhibition. It opens on 4 December 2026 and runs until 21 March 2027, spreading across heritage monuments, museums, galleries, embassies, institutions, streets and public spaces in Delhi. One Biennale Pass covers entry, with a one-day ticket at ₹100 and a season pass at ₹3,000. The pass carries a QR code and replaces the usual monument entry ticket at participating sites. Booking happens on the official booking page.

What Is the India Biennale 2026?

India Biennale '26, as the organizers style it, is the second edition of an exhibition that runs on a two-year cycle. A biennale is just a very large art show held every two years, and this one is mounted as a public-private partnership. The Ministry of Culture is a formal backer, with the stated aim of positioning India as a global center for artistic dialogue. That is lofty language for something fairly concrete: contemporary work placed inside some of Delhi's most recognizable heritage sites, so that art and architecture end up sharing the same space. The The official site is the hub for announcements.

When Does the India Biennale 2026 Open and Close?

Mark 4 December 2026 on the calendar. That is opening day, and the run continues through 21 March 2027. Those dates appear in Travel+Leisure Asia and Firstpost. A run of more than three months is generous, which matters if a December trip is not possible. The exhibition carries on well into the following March, so there is room to plan around other commitments.

Where Are the Biennale Venues in Delhi?

Forget the single white-cube gallery. This biennale deliberately scatters itself. Venues include heritage monuments, museums, galleries, embassies, institutions, streets and public spaces right across Delhi. That mix is the point: work turns up in formal exhibition rooms and in the middle of everyday city life. The complete list of Delhi venues is published by Travel+Leisure Asia, and the official exhibitions page tracks what is showing where. Because the sites are spread out, grouping visits by neighborhood saves a great deal of crossing the city.

What Does the Biennale Pass Actually Do?

This is the detail that catches people out. The Biennale Pass is a single ticket with a QR code. At participating monuments it replaces the regular entry ticket you would otherwise buy at the gate. The pass is therefore both your exhibition credential and your monument access in one. The booking page issues it online, and you show the code at each site. It is a tidy idea, but it does mean you should keep the pass on your phone or carry a printout, since every scan counts.

How Much Does a Biennale Pass Cost?

Here are the published rates in plain numbers. The Unstumbled, in a report dated 4 November 2026, lists four pass types. Every price in the table links to that report, so you can check the figure yourself.

Pass typePriceSuited to
One-day₹100A single focused day
Three-day₹200A short city break
Weekly₹400Spreading visits across a week
Season₹3,000Repeated visits over the full run

The arithmetic is worth doing. If you plan to visit on more than thirty separate days, the season pass at ₹3,000 costs less than buying one-day tickets at ₹100 each. For most visitors a three-day or weekly pass is the better value.

In India

The India angle is not an afterthought here; it is the premise. The Biennale is structured as a public-private partnership, and the Ministry of Culture is a formal backer. Government pages, including the Ministry of Culture India Biennale page and the IAAD 2026 page, set out that official framing. Passes are priced in rupees for a domestic audience: ₹100 for one day, ₹200 for three days, ₹400 for a week and ₹3,000 for the season. Booking takes place on the Indian government domain at indiabiennale.culture.gov.in/booking-ticket, not through a third-party seller. The exhibitions page is the place to check which shows are on before you commit to a date.

In Other Countries

Biennales are a global format, and India's version sits in a long lineage. The Venice Biennale in Italy, founded in 1895, is the oldest of the breed and alternates its art and architecture editions across odd and even years. In the United States, the Whitney Biennale in New York is the best-known example of the form, while the United Kingdom leans more on fairs and festivals than on one national biennale. Art Basel Miami Beach is the clearest commercial counterpoint to Delhi. It runs from 4 to 6 December 2026 and functions as a market where galleries sell to collectors, whereas the India Biennale is a curated exhibition built around public viewing. The two share a month on the calendar and very different purposes.

What Can Visitors Expect From the Exhibitions?

The official exhibitions page lists the program, but the broad shape is clear from the coverage. Expect contemporary work across painting, sculpture, photography, video, installation and performance. Indian and international artists share the bill, and a number of pieces respond to the specific Delhi settings, whether a monument courtyard or a public street. Since venues range from formal museums to open spaces, the experience changes as you move around the city. Read the venue notes before setting out, because a show in a public space asks something different of a viewer than one inside a gallery.

Why Does the Biennale Matter for Indian Art?

A second edition is still a young event, but the scale here is unusual. Placing contemporary art inside heritage monuments forces a conversation between old and new that a conventional gallery cannot easily stage. The public-private structure matters too: it puts state support and private money behind one project, with the explicit goal of making India a global center for artistic dialogue. For Indian artists, that means a platform alongside international peers, in front of curators and critics who might not otherwise make the trip. Whether the promise is fully met is a longer question, but the ambition is written into the official brief.

How Do I Book a Pass and Plan a Visit?

Start at the booking page on the official domain. Choose the pass type that matches your plans, pay online, and keep the QR code ready for each entry. The exhibitions page is worth reading before you pick a day, since it says what is on at which venue. Delhi's metro reaches many central sites, and clustering venues by area keeps travel time down. With a run extending to 21 March 2027, there is no need to cram everything into one weekend.

Frequently Asked Questions

What should I pack for a day of venue hopping?

Comfortable shoes matter more than anything else, since several sites reward slow walking. Carry water, a cap and some sun protection for the open-air stops, and add a light layer for early starts. A small power bank is useful when your phone is doing ticket duty all day.

Are guided tours or artist talks part of the program?

Public programs are a normal feature of a biennale of this size. Talks, walkthroughs and guided visits are usually posted on the exhibitions page as the run progresses, and many are free to attend. Slots for popular sessions can fill up, so check the schedule a few days ahead rather than on arrival.

Can I use the pass from a phone screen?

The QR code is designed to be scanned at the gate, so a phone screen normally works. Screens fail at the worst moment, though. A printed backup or a screenshot saved offline costs nothing and removes the risk of a dead battery at the entrance.

Is photography allowed inside the venues?

Rules differ from one venue to the next and often from one artwork to another. Look for signage at the room entrance and ask staff if it is unclear. Flash is commonly restricted near sensitive works, and some lenders prohibit images altogether.

When is the least crowded time to visit?

Weekdays generally draw smaller crowds than weekends, and opening week tends to be busier than the middle of the run. If your schedule is flexible, an early start on a weekday gives you the best chance of quiet rooms. Popular public-space installations are the exception, since they attract passers-by regardless of the hour.
